## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `61a4cdbf1f30155ffa53e25239722c5791af0ad0`
Local-runs: probe — `node scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs --base origin/main --head pr-29953` on the head: the gate refused to report a verdict (no `tsx` under this checkout, "an input it cannot produce is a red, never a skip"), so no verdict was taken from it; the dev's reported "registered flow-condition-type-mismatch-refused (new here)" is judged by hand below.
Scope: card #29926 and its two comments; PR #29953 body, files list, head check-runs; the full head diff; at `pr-29953`: `.changeset/29926-type-mismatch-outcome-per-role.md`, `.changeset/29904-type-mismatch-fail-closed.md` (still present), `packages/formula/src/{validate.ts,expression-refusal.ts,index.ts,validate.test.ts,expression-refusal-codes.test.ts}`, `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts` (ledger 1283–1340, `checkNullGuards` wrapper 2382–2408, `check` 2409–2480, `checkDeclaredPredicate` 2557–2585, flow node/edge/decision sites 2744–3015, rule loop 3166–3240), `packages/lint/src/validate-null-guards.ts` (85–95, 280–300, 739–775), `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts` (976–1090, 3330–3356, 3664, 3931), `packages/mcp/src/{mcp-http-tools.ts,mcp-validate-expression.test.ts,skill-md.ts}`, `packages/objectql/src/publish-type-mismatch-fail-closed.test.ts`, `packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts` (36–37, 342–359, 3620–3695), `packages/services/service-automation/src/dag-traversal.ts` (1072–1135 `evaluateCondition`), `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts` (6200–6250 start-condition gate), `packages/triggers/trigger-record-change/src/record-change-trigger.ts` (368–380), `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.{flow-condition,validation}-type-mismatch-refused.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/types.ts` (`SemanticMigration`), `packages/spec/src/automation/flow-trigger-kind.ts`; main at `21510bba`: `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts:3204`; `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` header; `AGENTS.md` (Post-Task Checklist, Touched `packages/spec`); `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/contract-review.md`; `docs/adr/0087-*.md` header. External inputs read as data: npm registry metadata and the published tarballs of `@objectstack/formula@18.3.0`, `@objectstack/lint@18.3.0`, `@objectstack/mcp@18.3.0` (dist + CHANGELOG, extracted into the scratchpad); GitHub releases `*@18.3.0` (target `83d7e4ae`); the `Release` workflow runs on main today.

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on PR body and changeset) + published spec path. Run in-seat as an isolated reviewer at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, fed the card, the PR and the head's check-runs only.

### ① Derived judgments
- **Accept-set narrowing at the author-time gate (record-triggered flow start / edge condition, `type-mismatch` warning → `error`).** Correct and correctly derived. `faultOutcomeOf({kind:'flow condition', recordTriggered})` returns `'run-fails'` only when `resolveFlowTriggerKind(flow) === 'record_change'` (start `config.triggerType` starts with `record-`, `flow-trigger-kind.ts:76`), and is passed to `check(...)` only on the top-level start node (`isTriggerGate`) and on edges — exactly the twin's sites (`checkFlowNullGuards`, #29026). Any other flow and any non-start node condition keep `undefined` → warning. Judged right.
- **Runtime outcome `run-fails` is what the engine does.** Verified: `dag-traversal.ts:1072+` `evaluateCondition` throws on a non-`ok` evaluation (ADR-0032 §1c, "NO silent fallback"); `engine.ts:6229` calls it for the start condition inside `execute()`'s `try`; `record-change-trigger.ts:371–379` catches the run failure and swallows it ("a flow failure must NEVER break the CRUD write that triggered it"). So the run fails at the condition and the write lands; the old "silently evaluates to null" text was false there. The new message is true.
- **Twin grading measured correctly.** The twin's wrapper always pushes `severity: 'error'` regardless of outcome (`validate-expressions.ts:2401`), passed `'run-fails'` on record-triggered start/edge/decision (`validate-null-guards.ts:93, 284–286`), and — on main `21510bba:3204` — called `checkNullGuards(..., objectName)` with the default `'fail-closed'` on every validation rule regardless of `severity`. So "the twin refuses advisory rules, worded fail-closed" is a correct measurement; the PR keeps the refusal and re-words both verdicts. Judged right.
- **Advisory-rule handling is truthful about runtime.** `rule-validator.ts:3630–3672`: `severity !== 'error'` → `evaluateRule(..., advisory: true)`; an unevaluable advisory violation is neither pushed to `errors` nor to `advisories`, only logged via `unevaluableAdvisoryMessage` ("write proceeded: the rule is advisory, so it was not applied to this write"). A nested `conditional` branch is governed by the outer rule's severity (`rule-validator.ts:36–37, 342–346`), matching the ledger's "a nested branch inherits it" and `ruleOutcome` applied to every predicate of the rule. The new `fail-open` clause ("skipped, not refused: the write proceeds, the rule is never applied… the only trace is a log line") matches. The twin's previously unused `'fail-open'` clause is re-worded for the surface that genuinely skips; the requiredWhen pins at test 3340–3353 assert its absence on fail-closed surfaces and still hold. Judged right.
- **Code split `type-mismatch` → `type-mismatch` (warning) + `type-mismatch-fail-closed` / `-run-fails` / `-fail-open` (errors), `outcome` param removed.** The code is right: `TYPE_MISMATCH_FAULT_ARMS` is keyed by `ExprFaultOutcome`, so a new outcome without a code does not compile; `CODE_TABLE` gains the three; `PINS` is typed over `ExpressionRefusalCode` so each has a pin; `SWEEP_SCHEMAS` carries the deal schema once per outcome. The fail-closed sentence is byte-identical to #29923's (checked against the shipped 18.3.0 dist string). **But the claim that this arm "has not shipped in a release" is false.** `@objectstack/formula@18.3.0` (published 2026-11-03T15:09Z; the `*@18.3.0` GitHub releases target `83d7e4ae`, the version-packages merge, of which #29923 `4c2cd29a` is an ancestor) carries `outcome: "fail-closed"` in `dist/index.{js,mjs}` and `readonly outcome?: 'fail-closed'` on `ExpressionRefusalParams['type-mismatch']` in `dist/index.d.ts`; `@objectstack/mcp@18.3.0` serves `faultOutcome: "fail-closed"` on the `validation` site, so an MCP consumer on 18.3.0 receives code `type-mismatch` with `params.outcome`; `@objectstack/lint@18.3.0` ships the fail-closed grading. The #29904 changeset is still in `.changeset/` only because the version-packages PR #26517 branched before #29923 merged, so 18.3.0's CHANGELOGs have no entry for it (0 mentions of 29904/29923 in the three shipped CHANGELOGs). Consequence: renaming the arm's code and deleting `params.outcome` is a narrowing of a **served** code and a served type, not an unreleased one. The PR **does** declare the rename inside its `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line and the FROM → TO carries the consumer mapping (`type-mismatch` + `params.outcome === 'fail-closed'` → `type-mismatch-fail-closed`), so the declaration is structurally complete; what is wrong is the premise ("尚未发版" in the maintainer brief, "has not shipped in a release" in the body) and the changeset's "Supersedes, in the same release" framing, which will ship in the next CHANGELOG as the claim that the `outcome` param was introduced and replaced in one release, when 18.3.0 has been serving it. Judged **wrong on the premise, right on the declaration** — see ④ and REWORK-1.
- **New exported type `ExprFaultOutcome` and two new codes** — widenings, correctly listed "beside" the narrowing and not counted as the arm. Right.
- **MCP `validate_expression`**: `validation` → `type-mismatch-fail-closed`, `flow_condition` → `type-mismatch-run-fails` error. The code is right; the derived claim "answers what the gate will" is only approximately true: the tool has no `severity` input, so an advisory rule's author is told fail-closed where the gate serves fail-open, and `flow_condition` always declares `run-fails` where the gate warns on a non-record-triggered flow. Pre-existing shape of the site map; flagged in ③, not blocking.
- **D3 entry text 200 → 201** — correct; the data door answers 201.

### ② Semver level
`minor` on `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/mcp`, `@objectstack/spec` — consistent with `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` (a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves). Every moved published package is listed: `packages/objectql` moves only in a test file (`publish-type-mismatch-fail-closed.test.ts`, not shipped), `content/docs` is not a package. Both line-initial declarations (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`) are present in the PR body and the changeset and agree. The changeset carries the **BREAKING** banner, the FROM → TO, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker `<!-- adr-0087: registered flow-condition-type-mismatch-refused -->`. `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are green on the head. Level judged right; the body's prose premise about the code rename is the defect (REWORK-1), not the level.

### ③ Boundary flags
- **Dev reading 1 — non-record-triggered flows keep the "evaluates to null" warning.** Agree it is out of this card (the card scopes item 1 to record-triggered flows and the twin has no grading there). The text is still false for them (same `evaluateCondition` throws). **File** as a follow-up; not blocking. Pin note: the new lint test titled "keeps the warning on a flow that is not record-triggered, and on an inert node condition" exercises only the inert node (its flow is `record-after-update`); the non-record case is actually pinned by the pre-existing "warns on a flattened flow condition doing arithmetic on a bare text field" (start node without `triggerType`). Retitle or add a `triggerType: 'scheduled'` case (should-fix, non-blocking).
- **Dev reading 2 — `record.x` in a flow condition is never type-judged.** Confirmed pre-existing (the flattened-scope soundness check types bare names only). **File**; not blocking.
- **Dev reading 3 — `decision` branches get no type verdict.** Confirmed: `checkDeclaredPredicate` (`validate-expressions.ts:2583`) calls `validateExpression('predicate', raw)` with no schema hint, so no `fieldTypes` and no `faultOutcome` reach a decision branch; the twin alone refuses there. **File** (a decision branch `name > 5` also fails the run and draws nothing); not blocking.
- **MCP site map cannot express severity or trigger kind** (`validation` always `fail-closed`, `flow_condition` always `run-fails`); the tool description and skill text say "where it refuses the write / fails the run" without that caveat. **File** against `packages/mcp`; not blocking.
- **Release-lane defect surfaced by this review, not this PR's:** 18.3.0 shipped #29923's narrowing (formula / lint / mcp / spec) without its changelog entry because the version-packages PR #26517 branched before `4c2cd29a` and was merged and released without regeneration. Needs a dedicated docs-only erratum for 18.3.0 and a check that a version-packages PR is regenerated against its merge-base before it lands. **File (p2) to the release lane.**
- No `open_questions` block on the PR beyond the three readings above. PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; PR is a draft, `mergeable_state: blocked`. Check-runs at review time: 22 completed success, 0 failed, 35 in progress (Test Core 1–8, Test UI 1–16, Type Check lanes, Build Core/Docs, Build & E2E UI); landing rule ② (all green) still owed by the lane at landing.

### ④ Narrowing face
- **FROM → TO** present and correct for the metadata narrowing: `name > 5` on a text field → `size(name) > 5` / `score > 5` on a number field / `double(name) > 5` only for numeric text; boolean `active > 0` → `active == true`; validated clean in the formula tests. For the code narrowing: `type-mismatch` + `params.outcome === 'fail-closed'` → `type-mismatch-fail-closed` — present. **Missing**: the statement that the FROM side is what `@objectstack/formula@18.3.0` / `@objectstack/mcp@18.3.0` serve (the body and brief say the opposite).
- **Disposition**: `registered flow-condition-type-mismatch-refused`; the id resolves to the new file `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.flow-condition-type-mismatch-refused.ts` and is new in the diff, so the `registered` arm's two conditions hold by inspection (gate probe refused to report here; dev reports it green and `Check Changeset` is green). `registry.ts` is generated and gitignored, so nothing further to commit for `packages/spec`.
- **D3 entry shape**: matches `SemanticMigration` (`id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`, no `conversionIds` because nothing mechanical is rewritten) and the sibling `18.validation-type-mismatch-refused` entry one for one; `surface` names the slots (`automation.Flow` start `config.condition`, `edges[].condition`, `triggerType record-*`), `reason` states the runtime fact that was verified above, `acceptanceCriteria` is a verify loop on `os validate` / `os build` / publish-drafts / a 201 create that runs past the condition. Judged right.
- **Migration path for authors**: the `error` lands at the slot path (`flows[0].nodes[0].config.condition`, `flows[0].edges[0].condition`) with the conversion named in the message; the door test proves the refusal through `saveMetaItem` + `publishPackageDrafts`. Adequate.
- **Pins / ablations**: adequate for the narrowing face — formula (`PINS` ×4 cases, `SWEEP_SCHEMAS` per outcome, `validate.test.ts` run-fails + fail-open), lint (record-triggered start+edge error, inert node warning, advisory `warning`/`info` incl. nested branch, twin agreement, `#5017` receiver table gains `rule.severity`), mcp (both sites), objectql door (advisory rule, record-triggered flow). Ablations A1–A5 each name the test that fails and A5 reproduces the card's premise through the built lint dist. One pin-title gap (③ reading 1). No gap on the served-code rename beyond the prose premise.

### Rework

1. **(blocking) The code rename is a served-code narrowing; "unreleased" is false.** `@objectstack/formula@18.3.0` (npm 2026-11-03T15:09Z) ships `type-mismatch` with `outcome: 'fail-closed'` (dist + `index.d.ts`, seat re-measured: 10 hits in `index.d.ts`); `@objectstack/mcp@18.3.0` serves it on the `validation` site. The #29904 changeset stayed pending only because version-packages #26517 branched before `4c2cd29a`. Fix: (a) changeset: replace "Supersedes, in the same release" with the truth (the arm shipped in 18.3.0 without a changelog line; this release renames `type-mismatch` + `params.outcome: 'fail-closed'` → `type-mismatch-fail-closed` and removes `outcome`), keep FROM → TO; (b) PR body: strike 尚未发版 / "has not shipped in a release", state the 18.3.0 consumer impact in 风险与回滚. Declaration lines, level and ADR-0087 marker unchanged.
2. (should-fix) Retitle or extend the lint test "keeps the warning on a flow that is not record-triggered, and on an inert node condition": its flow is `record-after-update`; add a `scheduled` / no-`triggerType` start+edge case.
3. Filed by the seat, not this PR: the 18.3.0 changelog gap (release lane), the three dev readings, the MCP site-map severity/trigger-kind gap.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-ddyc2k`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzibcN9oHa8kDbTTnL5`

**VERDICT: REWORK**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `06abf5acf76683083d0ef57c5a0d7af70053f4fa`
Local-runs: none
Scope: delta review of rework r1 against the full review at `61a4cdbf1f30155ffa53e25239722c5791af0ad0` (one commit, `git diff 61a4cdbf..06abf5ac`: `.changeset/29926-type-mismatch-outcome-per-role.md` +1/−1, `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts` +28/−1); the corrected PR body draft at `/mnt/project-files/issue-29926/pr-body-r1.md` (not yet live; the live head is `06abf5ac`, draft PR); `packages/spec/src/automation/flow-trigger-kind.ts:64–85` (re-read for the `schedule` arm); the new head's check-runs (2 success, 2 skipped, 5 in progress, 0 failed at review time). Everything else carries over from the review at `61a4cdbf`, which read the whole diff, the runtime, the twin, the ADR-0087 gate, the D3 entries and the published 18.3.0 tarballs.

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on PR body and changeset) + published spec path. Run in-seat as an isolated reviewer at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, fed the card, the PR and the head's check-runs only.

### ① Derived judgments
- **REWORK-1 (served-code rename premise).** Fixed. The changeset's "Supersedes, in the same release" paragraph is replaced by "The renamed code shipped in 18.3.0": it states that `@objectstack/formula@18.3.0` and `@objectstack/mcp@18.3.0` already serve #29904's refusal as `type-mismatch` with `params.outcome: 'fail-closed'`, that the `outcome` param is in the 18.3.0 `ExpressionRefusalParams` type, that 18.3.0's changelog has no line for it because `29904-type-mismatch-fail-closed.md` was not consumed by that release, and that this release renames the arm and removes the param so an 18.3.0 consumer moves to `type-mismatch-fail-closed` via the FROM → TO. Every one of those statements matches what I measured on the published tarballs and the `*@18.3.0` release target `83d7e4ae`. The "flow conditions keep the warning" supersession is kept as a separate, true sentence. The corrected body strikes the "has not shipped" bullet with a bracketed r1 edit stating the same facts, and 风险与回滚 now tells the maintainer that the arm shipped in 18.3.0 and that a consumer keyed to `type-mismatch` + `outcome` must move to the new code. Judged right.
- **REWORK-2 (mis-titled pin).** Fixed. The old test is split: "keeps the warning on a flow that is not record-triggered: start and edge conditions" now runs two flows — a start with no `triggerType` and a start with `schedule: '0 * * * *'` — and asserts `warning` on both the start `condition` and the edge `condition`. Under `resolveFlowTriggerKind` neither is `record_change` (no `record-*` `triggerType`; `config.schedule != null` → `'schedule'`), so `nullGuardObject` is undefined, `faultOutcomeOf` declares nothing, and the verdict stays the warning while `objectName` still binds `title` for the type check. "keeps the warning on an inert node condition of a record-triggered flow" keeps the original record-triggered inert-node body under a title that says what it exercises. The non-record branch of `faultOutcomeOf` is now pinned on both sites, so forcing `recordTriggered: true` would fail a named test. Judged right.
- All other derived judgments (narrowing sites, `run-fails` runtime, twin grading, advisory `fail-open` wording, code split, MCP, D3 200 → 201) carry over unchanged: the delta touches no source file.

### ② Semver level
Unchanged: `minor` ×4 on `@objectstack/formula` / `lint` / `mcp` / `spec`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` line-initial and identical in the changeset and the corrected body, **BREAKING** banner, FROM → TO and the single marker `<!-- adr-0087: registered flow-condition-type-mismatch-refused -->` untouched by the delta. The dev reports `check-adr-0087-registration`, `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-empty-changeset` exit 0 on r1; the earlier head's `Check Changeset` was green and the changeset's frontmatter and declaration lines did not move. Carries over as right.

### ③ Boundary flags
- Carry over, unchanged, as **file** items (none blocking): non-record-triggered flows keep a warning whose "evaluates to null" text is still false there (now at least pinned as the intended behaviour); `record.x` in a flow condition is never type-judged; `decision` branches receive no type verdict; the MCP site map cannot express a rule's `severity` or a flow's trigger kind; the release-lane defect that 18.3.0 shipped #29923 without its changelog entry (version-packages #26517 branched before `4c2cd29a`) — needs a docs-only 18.3.0 erratum and a regenerate-before-land guard, not this PR.
- The corrected PR body is not live yet; the seat writes it through the relay. The record below is on the head; the body's declaration lines are unchanged from the live body, so the write is prose only.
- Check-runs on `06abf5ac` at review time: 2 success, 2 skipped, 5 in progress, 0 failed. Landing rule ② (all green) is still owed by the lane at landing. PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; PR is a draft.

### ④ Narrowing face
- FROM → TO: unchanged and complete for the metadata narrowing (`size(name) > 5` / number field / `double(name) > 5` / `active == true`) and for the served code (`type-mismatch` + `params.outcome === 'fail-closed'` → `type-mismatch-fail-closed`); the delta adds the missing fact that the FROM side is what 18.3.0 serves, so an upgrading agent grepping the CHANGELOG learns it is renaming a code it runs today. Judged right.
- Disposition `registered flow-condition-type-mismatch-refused`, D3 entry shape, migration path and pins/ablations carry over from `61a4cdbf`; the one pin gap named there is closed by the split test. No new gap introduced.

## 席位核对

Verdict: **ACCEPT** at head `06abf5acf76683083d0ef57c5a0d7af70053f4fa` · 2026-11-03T17:39Z

- **Shape:** 16 files: formula verdict and refusal codes, the lint `faultOutcomeOf` ledger, the MCP `validate_expression` site map, a new D3 semantic entry under `packages/spec/src/migrations`, docs, and one minor changeset. Narrowing face + published spec path ⇒ `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`. The first review, 6610931370 at `61a4cdbf`, was REWORK: the renamed code had shipped in 18.3.0. Rework r1 is PASS 6611149064 at this head.
- **Premise measured:** the dev reproduced it through the built lint dist (ablation A5: the record-triggered flow published with the false "evaluates to null" warning). The runtime fact behind `run-fails` was verified by the reviewer: `evaluateCondition` throws, and the record-change trigger swallows the run failure while the write lands.
- **Gates:** `dispatch-gates` 106/106 exit 0, suites green for formula 1634, lint 7953, mcp 660 and spec 24277 + 1524. `pnpm lint` exit 0. The changeset gates were rerun on r1 with exit 0. Landing waits for every check on this head to be green or an expected skip.
- **Accepted deviations:** harness-pinned branch `claude/project-thread-ddyc2k`. The body was rewritten by the seat through the relay with the r1 text, plus the signed trailer.
- **Out of scope, where it goes:** the seat files these follow-ups: the 18.3.0 changelog gap (release lane), non-record-triggered flow-condition wording, `record.x` never type-judged, `decision` branches with no type verdict, and the MCP site map's missing severity / trigger kind.
- **Landing:** on all-green at this head, the seat sends `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` through the relay.
